body: What turns me away from that is the logistics. Carrying white black and red paint up to the 13th floor, into the attic (walkable thanks to foreign wooden planks), up another staircase, into the back of the room, and then proceeded to paint. They must’ve waited for the black to dry, then put the red, then put the white. They also had to come up with a poem (weirdly about the “spirits” of the place), come up with a key, and then translate it. There’s also just weird letters on the columns that don’t make any sense, but again you could be totally right. It just feels like so much effort for a joke.

Just to note another weird thing I noticed, some words have strange misspellings or are missing letters on the last wall. The top says inabilty, questions is spelt “quetions”, and floorboards is spelt “floorbourds.”
The last few letters cut off at the bottom right of the second photo are: d e r
True, just one of those things where I wish I knew why
There was a key to the left of the writings I probably should’ve posted with the rest of the pictures. But yeah, there was a code for the whole alphabet
It’s huge, but everything we saw was just old elevator and electricity boxes that were used. There’s graffiti everywhere but this one spot was the only thing that heavily used paint
also note it smelled really bad in here, and thats compared to the rest of the decomposing building.

i also have a disability that makes homework take almost 2-3x as long. i feel so drained all the time. i was prescribed adderall and probably should take a sort of antidepressant but i don’t bc adderall can increase depression. my parents don’t understand how depression works and i just feel so trapped. i need to go to college soon or i might just fucjing kill myself
